core_obligations: Statement (lines 4710-4716): if F : A -> B is a functor between differential graded categories over R satisfying axioms (A), (B), (C), and F(x[1]) = F(x)[1], then F induces an exact functor K(A) -> K(B) of triangulated categories.

Preservation of admissible sequences (proof lines 4716-4718): an admissible short exact sequence x -> y -> z in Comp(A) is a termwise-split sequence whose graded biproduct structure and differentials are preserved by the additive (R-linear) functor F, so F(x) -> F(y) -> F(z) is an admissible short exact sequence in Comp(B).

Boundary compatibility (lines 4718-4727): the boundary morphism delta = pi d(s) of the source sequence is sent to F(delta) : F(z) -> F(x[1]) = F(x)[1], and by functoriality F(delta) = F(pi) d(F(s)), which is exactly the boundary morphism of the image admissible short exact sequence; hence the distinguished triangle of the image sequence is the image of the original one, and F extends to an exact functor of homotopy categories.
proof_roadmap: Preserve the admissible short exact sequences through the additive functor.
Transport the boundary morphism using F(x[1]) = F(x)[1].
Conclude the induced functor on homotopy categories is exact.
difficulty_reason: Exact-functor lemma (statement 4710-4716, proof 4716-4727): a functor between ABC-category differential graded categories compatible with shifts induces an exact functor of homotopy categories - the proof carries the admissible short exact sequences through F and checks the boundary morphism agreement explicitly (F(delta) = F(pi) d(F(s))); the preservation of admissible sequences is the standard additivity argument for R-linear functors, compressed in the source to a single assertion with the mechanism transparent. H2: short functoriality argument.
